newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chernomyrdin takes break despite Yeltsin illness.
newsitem.headline: Chernomyrdin takes break despite Yeltsin illness.

text.p: Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin has begun a short holiday, his office said on Thursday, a day after President Boris Yeltsin was taken to hospital with signs of pneumonia.

"The prime minister is on holiday from today," a spokeswoman for Chernomyrdin said by telephone. She said she did not know where Chernomyrdin, Yeltsin's constitutional number two, would be during his time off.
First Deputy Prime Minister Aleksei Bolshakov said later on Thursday Chernomyrdin was spending his break near Moscow and was in close touch with his government colleagues.

"The head of the Russian government Viktor Chernomyrdin, on a short holiday which he is spending near Moscow, is controlling the situation and maintaining close ties with us," Interfax news agency quoted Bolshakov as telling a government meeting.

Chernomyrdin, who would step in temporarily if Yeltsin became incapacitated, briefly took control of the state, including Russia's nuclear arsenal, when the Kremlin leader underwent heart bypass surgery on November 5.
